title: High-throughput Generative Inference of Large Language Models with a Single GPU (FlexGen)
technique: offloading across GPU/CPU/disk with LP-searched tensor placement and zig-zag block schedule, plus 4-bit weight and KV compression

optimized_metrics.evidence: this paper initiates the study of high-throughput LLM inference using limited resources, such as a single commodity GPU. We present FlexGen, a high-throughput generation engine
At any time, the total size of tensors stored on a device cannot exceed its memory capacity.
FlexGen further compresses the weights and the attention cache to 4 bits with negligible accuracy loss.
can be easily extended to incorporate latency and throughput constraints, thus helping to navigate the trade-off space smoothly
optimized_metrics.locator: §1 (optional latency bound in the policy search)

headline_claim.text: FlexGen achieves 100x higher maximum throughput for OPT-175B on a single T4 (effective batch size 144) than DeepSpeed Zero-Inference / Hugging Face Accelerate, at higher latency

reported_metrics.where: Fig 1 latency vs throughput, Table 2 block latency

metric_definitions.definition_quote: the latency t is defined as the total number of seconds spent to process the prompts and generate all the bn tokens.
metric_definitions.notes: latency of a whole batch (block), not per-request; thousands of seconds

metric_definitions.definition_quote: The generation throughput is defined as bn/t.
metric_definitions.notes: b = effective batch size, n = output length: counts generated tokens only; prompt processing time is in t

load_regime: offline batch; effective batch size and block size chosen by policy search; latency-throughput frontier plotted
tradeoff_acknowledged: latency sacrificed for throughput (e.g. latency 5000s to 12000s at 69-100x throughput)
hardware: NVIDIA T4 16GB, 208GB CPU DRAM, 1.5TB SSD; also 4xT4 for decentralized comparison
workloads: synthetic prompt length 512 and output 32/128 tokens; HELM benchmark; Wikitext
extractor_notes: Explicitly throughput-oriented, latency-insensitive. Policy search LP objective is throughput (minimizing total execution time for a block).
